articles.title: How to Build a Weekly Rhythm You Can Actually Keep
articles.excerpt: Discipleship dies in the gap between good intentions and the calendar. A rhythm you can keep beats an ambitious one you'll abandon by March.

articles.title: How to Disciple One Person Over Coffee
articles.excerpt: Not everyone needs a table of twelve. Sometimes discipleship is one person, one standing appointment, and a long obedience built one cup at a time.

articles.title: How to Make Disciples When You Feel Unqualified
articles.excerpt: The sense that you're not ready is not a reason to wait. It is, strangely, the very condition Jesus has always worked with.

articles.title: How to Multiply a Table by Sending People to Start Their Own
articles.excerpt: A table that only grows is a crowd. A table that multiplies is a movement. Here is how to send people out before you feel ready to let them go.

articles.title: How to Open the Bible With People Who Have Never Read It
articles.excerpt: For the friend who has never cracked a Bible, where you start and how you read it matters more than anything you say about it.

articles.title: How to Pray With People Without It Being Awkward
articles.excerpt: Praying out loud with others terrifies most people. A few simple habits take the performance out of it and leave the honesty in.

articles.title: How to Start a Discipleship Table This Week
articles.excerpt: You do not need a curriculum, a building, or a title. You need a table, a meal, and the willingness to start before you feel ready.

articles.title: How to Welcome a Skeptic to Your Table
articles.excerpt: A doubter at your table is not a threat to it. Welcomed well, the skeptic keeps the table honest and may find, as I did, that belief is more lived than argued into.

articles.title: The Three Questions That Make Any Passage Teachable
articles.excerpt: You do not need a commentary or a seminary degree. You need three questions you can ask of any text, and the discipline to let the room answer them.

articles.title: What to Actually Do at a Discipleship Table
articles.excerpt: A simple, repeatable shape for the evening — eat, open the Word, pray, send — so you are never wondering what comes next.

articles.title: What to Do When No One Comes Back
articles.excerpt: You opened your home, set the table, and the next week the chairs were empty. Before you quit, consider what the silence is and isn't telling you.

articles.title: Who to Invite to Your Table (and How to Ask)
articles.excerpt: Stop looking for strangers to evangelize. Look at the names already in your phone, and learn to ask in a way that opens a door instead of triggering an alarm.

articles.title: How to Answer Hard Questions About the Faith
articles.excerpt: You do not need every answer. You need honesty, a little courage, and the willingness to say the three words most Christians are afraid to say.

articles.title: How to Be a Good Neighbor on Your Street
articles.excerpt: Your street is a parish you did not choose. Faithfulness there is slow, ordinary, and more powerful than any program.

articles.title: How to Disagree Without Losing the Relationship
articles.excerpt: We are losing friendships over arguments at a rate our parents would not recognize. Here is how to hold your convictions and keep your people.

articles.title: How to Invite Someone to a Table or a Church
articles.excerpt: The invitation is the hardest sentence to say and the easiest thing to overthink. Here is how to actually open the door.

articles.title: How to Live a Quiet Witness at Work
articles.excerpt: Most workplace evangelism is either obnoxious or invisible. There is a steadier way, and it is mostly about how you do your job and treat your people.

articles.title: How to Love Your Actual Neighbors
articles.excerpt: We talk about loving humanity while not knowing the names of the people on our own street. Jesus made the neighbor specific on purpose.

articles.title: How to Pray for People Who Do Not Believe
articles.excerpt: Before evangelism is a word you say, it is a prayer you carry. Praying for the people who do not believe changes them less predictably than it changes you.

articles.title: How to Share Your Faith Without Being Weird
articles.excerpt: Most of us are either silent or strange. There is a third way, and it looks more like Jesus than either of the first two.

articles.title: How to Show Hospitality to Outsiders
articles.excerpt: The table is where the gospel becomes visible. Hospitality to outsiders is not entertaining. It is the open door of a people who were let in.

articles.title: How to Talk About Jesus With Your Family
articles.excerpt: Family is the hardest mission field and the one we most often give up on. The people who knew you before are exactly the ones who can see whether it is real.

articles.title: How to Tell Your Story
articles.excerpt: You do not need a dramatic conversion to have a story worth telling. You need to be honest about what was broken and what is different now.

articles.title: How to Welcome a Stranger
articles.excerpt: Scripture keeps insisting we welcome the stranger because we were strangers once. Hospitality to outsiders is not a personality trait. It is an obedience.

articles.title: How to Bless Your Home and Your Children
articles.excerpt: Speaking blessing over your children is not superstition. It is a parent doing what God has always done: naming a person, and speaking a good future over them out loud.

articles.title: How to Build Family Traditions That Form Faith
articles.excerpt: Children are formed less by what you say once than by what you do every year. A tradition is a sermon you preach with your hands, repeated until it becomes their bones.

articles.title: How to Disciple Teenagers at Home
articles.excerpt: Discipling a teenager is not running a tighter program. It is staying in the room when they pull away, answering the hard question instead of dodging it, and refusing to outsource their faith.

articles.title: How to Eat Dinner Together Again
articles.excerpt: The shared table is where a family is built or quietly lost. Most homes did not decide to stop eating together. They drifted, one busy night at a time.

articles.title: How to Keep Advent as a Family
articles.excerpt: Advent is not a countdown to presents. It is four weeks of teaching your children to wait in the dark for a light that is coming, which is the whole shape of the Christian life.

articles.title: How to Keep Lent and Easter as a Family
articles.excerpt: Lent teaches a child to give something up so that Easter can mean something. You cannot rise on Sunday if you never walked the road to Friday.

articles.title: How to Make a Family Screen Covenant
articles.excerpt: Screens are not neutral. They form your children whether or not you decide they should. A covenant is how a family decides on purpose instead of drifting by default.

articles.title: How to Open Your Home in Hospitality as a Family
articles.excerpt: Hospitality is not entertaining. It is opening your ordinary home to people who need it, and letting your children grow up watching the table get longer.

articles.title: How to Pray With Your Kids at Bedtime
articles.excerpt: Bedtime is the one moment a child is finally still. Use it to teach them that the last voice before sleep speaks to a Father who never sleeps.

articles.title: How to Read the Bible With Young Children
articles.excerpt: You do not need a curriculum or a clever method. You need to open the book, read a little, and let your children watch you take it seriously.

articles.title: How to Start Family Worship (and Keep It When It Falls Apart)
articles.excerpt: Family worship is not a performance you have to be qualified for. It is a few honest minutes around a table, kept badly for years, until it becomes the air your children breathe.

articles.title: How to Use a Family Catechism
articles.excerpt: A catechism is not a test. It is a set of true sentences, learned by heart in childhood, that surface decades later when a person needs them most.

articles.title: How to Actually Forgive Your Spouse
articles.excerpt: Forgiveness is not pretending it did not happen, and it is not a feeling that arrives on its own. It is a decision, often made before the feeling catches up.

articles.title: How to Fight Fair
articles.excerpt: The goal of a marital argument is not to win. A marriage where someone keeps winning is a marriage where someone keeps losing.

articles.title: How to Handle In-Laws (Leaving and Cleaving)
articles.excerpt: Much marital misery is really an unfinished leaving. A man shall leave his father and mother, and we skip that verb in our hurry to the next one.

articles.title: How to Have a Weekly Marriage Check-In
articles.excerpt: Most marriages do not die in a blowup. They die in a hundred small things never said. A weekly check-in is how you keep the silence from accumulating.

articles.title: How to Have the Money Conversation Without a War
articles.excerpt: Money fights are almost never about money. They are about fear and control and worth, and a budget cannot fix a thing the budget cannot see.

articles.title: How to Know When to Get Help
articles.excerpt: Most couples wait far too long to get help, treating counseling as the last stop before the lawyer. The wisest couples go early, while there is still warmth to build on.

articles.title: How to Love a Spouse Who Has Gone Cold
articles.excerpt: When a marriage goes cold from one side, the temptation is to match the coldness. The harder and better road is to keep loving without a guarantee.

articles.title: How to Pray Together as a Couple
articles.excerpt: Couples who long to pray together often do not, because the first attempt felt awkward and exposed. The awkwardness is the doorway, not the wall.

articles.title: How to Protect a Weekly Date Night
articles.excerpt: Date night fails not because couples do not value it, but because everything else is louder. Protecting it is a discipline, not a romance.

articles.title: How to Rekindle Desire in a Long Marriage
articles.excerpt: Desire in a long marriage does not die because love faded. It cools because the conditions that fed it quietly disappeared, and the conditions can be rebuilt.

articles.title: How to Repair After a Blowup
articles.excerpt: Every marriage has bad fights. The ones that last are not the couples who never cross the line. They are the ones who come back fast.

articles.title: How to Stay Married in the Baby Years
articles.excerpt: No one warns you that the baby can come between you. The child does not threaten the marriage, but the way we organize our love around the child often does.

articles.title: How to Answer Your Child's Hard Questions About God
articles.excerpt: When your child asks a question you cannot answer, the answer they most need is not certainty. It is a parent who will not flinch and will not lie.

articles.title: How to Apologize to Your Kids
articles.excerpt: A parent who apologizes is not undermining their authority. They are teaching the one lesson about grace that no sermon can deliver.

articles.title: How to Bless Your Children
articles.excerpt: Your children are listening for one thing underneath everything else: whether you delight in them. Blessing is how you say it out loud, on purpose, again and again.

articles.title: How to Discipline in a Way That Reaches the Heart
articles.excerpt: Most discipline manages behavior and never touches the heart underneath it. Reaching the heart is slower, harder, and the only thing that lasts.

articles.title: How to Have the Screen Conversation by Age
articles.excerpt: The screen conversation is not one talk. It is a different conversation at five, at ten, at fifteen, and the version that works changes as fast as the child does.

articles.title: How to Help an Anxious Child
articles.excerpt: An anxious child does not need their fear erased or argued away. They need a steady adult to borrow calm from until they grow their own.

articles.title: How to Lead Your Family When You Feel Like a Failure
articles.excerpt: The qualification to lead your family was never your competence. It is your willingness to keep showing up, repenting, and pointing past yourself to God.

articles.title: How to Parent a Strong-Willed Child
articles.excerpt: The strong will that exhausts you at six may be the spine that saves your child at sixteen. The work is to shape it, not to break it.

articles.title: How to Raise Kids Who Own Their Faith
articles.excerpt: You cannot hand your child a faith they merely inherit. You can only raise them in conditions where a faith of their own has room to grow.

articles.title: How to Start Family Worship in Five Minutes
articles.excerpt: Family worship is not a production. It is a few honest minutes around a table, repeated until it becomes the air your children breathe.

articles.title: How to Stay Close to a Teenager Who Is Pulling Away
articles.excerpt: A teenager pulling away is doing exactly what they are supposed to do. The work is to stay reachable without chasing, present without smothering.

articles.title: How to Talk to Your Kids About Sex
articles.excerpt: The sex talk is not a single dreaded event but a long, ordinary conversation. If you do not have it, the culture and the search bar will have it for you.

articles.title: How to Be Content When You Long to Be Married
articles.excerpt: Contentment is not pretending you do not want the thing. It is the harder, truer work of being whole while you wait, with the longing still alive.

articles.title: How to Build Deep Friendships as an Adult
articles.excerpt: Most adults are lonely and would never say so. Friendship does not happen to grown-ups by accident anymore. You have to build it on purpose.

articles.title: How to Date With Wisdom
articles.excerpt: Most dating advice is either too casual or too anxious. There is a third way, slower than the culture and warmer than the rulebook.

articles.title: How to Find a Mentor
articles.excerpt: Most people wait to be chosen by a mentor and never are. Mentoring is not a program you get assigned to. It is a relationship you go and build.

articles.title: How to Forgive Someone Who Has Not Apologized
articles.excerpt: Waiting for an apology that may never come hands the offender control of your healing. Forgiveness is something you can do without their permission.

articles.title: How to Handle a Breakup
articles.excerpt: A breakup is a small death, and we keep telling people to get over it like it was a head cold. Grief that is rushed does not heal. It hides.

articles.title: How to Handle Loneliness
articles.excerpt: Loneliness is not a character flaw and it is not always solved by being around people. It is a signal, and the question is what you do with it.

articles.title: How to Have a Hard Conversation
articles.excerpt: The conversation you keep avoiding is usually the one that would heal the thing. Avoidance is not peace. It is just slower damage.

articles.title: How to Know If You Should Marry Someone
articles.excerpt: Nobody arrives at this decision with certainty. But there is a difference between healthy uncertainty and the doubt you are training yourself to ignore.

articles.title: How to Love a Difficult Family Member
articles.excerpt: You cannot choose your family and you cannot fix them. But you can decide how you will love them, which is a different and more possible thing.

articles.title: How to Set Healthy Boundaries With In-Laws
articles.excerpt: Leave and cleave is not a suggestion. A marriage needs a fence around it, and building that fence kindly is one of the first jobs of a new family.

articles.title: How to Thrive as a Single Christian
articles.excerpt: Singleness is not a waiting room. The church has often treated it that way, and single people have often believed it. Both were wrong.

articles.title: How to Actually Read the Bible
articles.excerpt: Most people do not stop reading the Bible because they decided it was false. They stop because they opened to Leviticus in January and quietly gave up by Leviticus 11.

articles.title: How to Build a Rule of Life
articles.excerpt: A rule of life is not a list of religious obligations. It is a trellis. It is the structure that holds your soul in place long enough for something to grow on it.

articles.title: How to Confess Sin and Walk in Repentance
articles.excerpt: Confession is not groveling to a God who is reluctant to forgive. It is the daily, ordinary practice of telling the truth to a Father who is running toward you before you finish the sentence.

articles.title: How to Deal With Anger
articles.excerpt: Anger is not the sin. What you do in the four seconds after the anger arrives is the sin, or the saint. The whole battle is fought in those four seconds.

articles.title: How to Examine Your Day (the Daily Examen)
articles.excerpt: Most of us end the day by collapsing, not by looking. The examen is the ancient practice of looking back over a single day with God before the dark takes it from you.

articles.title: How to Fast
articles.excerpt: Fasting is not a hunger strike against God to make him answer. It is the deliberate emptying of the body to remind the soul what it actually hungers for.

articles.title: How to Fight Anxiety With Scripture
articles.excerpt: You cannot argue yourself out of anxiety. But you can preach to yourself, and the question is only which voice gets the last word, your fear or the word of God.

articles.title: How to Keep a Sabbath
articles.excerpt: Sabbath is not a reward for finishing your work. The work is never finished. Sabbath is the weekly declaration that the world will keep turning without you, because it was never being held up by you.

articles.title: How to Keep Going When God Feels Distant
articles.excerpt: The dry season is not a sign you have failed. It is a normal part of following God, and almost everyone who has gone deep with him has walked through it.

articles.title: How to Memorize Scripture
articles.excerpt: We memorize song lyrics by accident and Scripture not at all, then wonder why fear has a fuller vocabulary than faith when the hard hour comes.

articles.title: How to Practice Silence and Solitude
articles.excerpt: We have made noise our medication. Silence terrifies us because in the quiet we finally hear what we have been outrunning, and that is exactly why we need it.

articles.title: How to Pray When You Do Not Feel Like It
articles.excerpt: The advice to pray only when you feel moved would empty every prayer closet on earth by Wednesday. Prayer is not a mood. It is a relationship, and relationships are kept by showing up.

articles.title: How to Care for a Dying Loved One
articles.excerpt: Walking someone toward death is among the holiest and hardest things a person can do. It will cost you more than you have, and it is worth all of it.

articles.title: How to Face a Hard Diagnosis
articles.excerpt: The day the news comes, the floor drops out. You cannot control the disease. You can decide, slowly, how you will walk through what it asks of you.

articles.title: How to Find Hope When Nothing Changes
articles.excerpt: Some suffering does not end. The prayer goes unanswered for years. Here is how to find a hope that does not depend on the circumstance finally turning.

articles.title: How to Grieve Well
articles.excerpt: Grief is not a problem to be solved or a stage to be cleared. It is love with nowhere to go. The work is not to get over it. The work is to carry it.

articles.title: How to Handle Doubt
articles.excerpt: Doubt is not the opposite of faith. Often it is the growing pains of a faith outgrowing the answers it was handed as a child. Here is how to hold it honestly.

articles.title: How to Help a Friend Through Loss
articles.excerpt: You will be tempted to find the right words and stay away until you do. The right words are not the point. Showing up, badly and repeatedly, is the point.

articles.title: How to Hold Onto Faith in the Dark
articles.excerpt: Sometimes God goes silent and the lights go out and everything you believed feels like a story you told yourself. Here is how the saints have stayed when faith ran on fumes.

articles.title: How to Keep Going Through Depression
articles.excerpt: Depression lies, and it lies in your own voice. When the dark mind tells you to stop, here is how to keep putting one foot in front of the other, and where to get real help.

articles.title: How to Practice Lament
articles.excerpt: Lament is the prayer the modern church forgot. It is not unbelief and it is not whining. It is the language faith speaks when the world is broken and God seems silent.

articles.title: How to Pray When You Are Falling Apart
articles.excerpt: When you most need to pray you can least manage it. The good news the church often forgets: prayer was never about having the words. It was about turning your face.

articles.title: How to Sit With Someone Who Is Suffering
articles.excerpt: The instinct is to fix, to explain, to make the pain smaller so we can stand it. Almost everything that helps requires us to do less and stay longer.

articles.title: How to Wait on God
articles.excerpt: Waiting is not the empty space between God's acts. In Scripture it is one of his primary works in a person, and the hardest one to receive.

articles.title: How to Age With Grace
articles.excerpt: Our culture handles aging by hiding it or fighting it with ever more elaborate programs of postponement. Christians can simply look at it, grieving what it takes without grieving as those who have no hope.

articles.title: How to Build Rhythms of Work and Rest
articles.excerpt: We are the first society with no shared rhythm of rest, no hour when it is collectively bedtime and no day when it is collectively Sabbath. Nobody is handing the pattern back. It has to be rebuilt.

articles.title: How to Care for Your Body in Sickness
articles.excerpt: Sickness strips away the lie that you are in control. It is not a punishment to be ashamed of or a problem to be willed away, but a season to be received, with real medical help and a faith that can rest.

articles.title: How to Eat and Feast Without Guilt or Excess
articles.excerpt: Almost none of us simply eat. We manage, we reward, we punish, we apologize. The table was meant to be a place of gratitude and communion before it was ever a matter of nutrition.

articles.title: How to Face Your Own Limits Without Despair
articles.excerpt: You are a creature, and creatures come with edges. The need to sleep, to rest, to stop, is not a design flaw to engineer around. It is a built-in rehearsal of humility, and a gift.

articles.title: How to Honor Your Body as a Christian
articles.excerpt: The body is not a cage the soul is trapped in, and it is not the whole of who you are. It is a good gift, made and bought and bound for resurrection.

articles.title: How to Live With Chronic Pain and Faith
articles.excerpt: Chronic pain is the suffering the church understands least, because it does not resolve. Faith here is not a cure but a way to keep trusting God inside a body that hurts and will not stop.

articles.title: How to Move Your Body as Worship
articles.excerpt: Movement offered as gratitude for a working body is worship. Movement driven by punishment, fear, or the mirror is something else. The difference is everything.

articles.title: How to Receive Rest as a Gift, Not a Reward
articles.excerpt: Most of us only let ourselves rest once the work is done and the rest is earned. But the work is never done, and rest was never a wage. It is a gift, given before you have produced a thing.

articles.title: How to Sleep Like a Creature Who Trusts God
articles.excerpt: Sleep is not lost productivity. It is a nightly act of trust, hours of unconsciousness in which you admit that God runs the world and you do not.

articles.title: How to Steward Your Health
articles.excerpt: Health is not yours to optimize and it is not yours to neglect. It is a trust, held loosely, cared for as a gift and surrendered when it goes, without idolizing it and without despising it.

articles.title: How to Unhook From Your Screens
articles.excerpt: The phone is a factory whistle that never stops blowing. Attention is a form of love, and you are giving yours, all day, to a device engineered to take it.

articles.title: How to Be a Faithful Citizen
articles.excerpt: Scripture makes you a resident alien, a citizen of heaven who loves the country he does not worship. That is not a contradiction. It is the only way to be a citizen without becoming an idolater.

articles.title: How to Be In the World But Not Of It
articles.excerpt: Jesus prayed that we would stay in the world without belonging to it. We keep failing in both directions, fleeing the world or being absorbed by it. There is a third way, and he prayed for it.

articles.title: How to Care for Creation as a Christian
articles.excerpt: The first job God gave a human being was to tend a garden. Caring for creation is not a borrowed cause from the culture. It is the oldest assignment in the Bible.

articles.title: How to Care for the Poor Without Condescension
articles.excerpt: The poor do not need your pity, your savior complex, or your theory about why they are poor. They need to be treated as what they are, image-bearers owed dignity, not problems to be managed.

articles.title: How to Disagree About Politics With People You Love
articles.excerpt: We are losing marriages, friendships, and family over elections, at a rate our grandparents would not recognize. Here is how to keep your convictions and keep your people.

articles.title: How to Engage Politics Without Losing Your Soul
articles.excerpt: You can care about justice without making a kingdom of this world your god. The ancient creed that got Christians killed was political, and it set them free.

articles.title: How to Handle Money in an Affluent Society
articles.excerpt: Jesus said more about money than almost anything else, and almost none of it is comfortable for the comfortable. Handling money well begins by admitting how much it already handles you.

articles.title: How to Hold Justice and Mercy Together
articles.excerpt: The tribes each keep half and call it the whole. Scripture refuses to let you choose between justice and mercy, because God never did.

articles.title: How to Love Your Enemy
articles.excerpt: It is the command we admire from a safe distance and refuse to practice up close. Jesus did not mean love your enemy in theory. He meant the person you actually cannot stand.

articles.title: How to Resist Consumerism
articles.excerpt: The whole machine runs on convincing you that you are not yet complete. Resisting it is not about hating things. It is about refusing to let things tell you who you are.

articles.title: How to Seek the Good of Your City
articles.excerpt: God told his exiles to seek the welfare of the very city that had carried them off. Your city is not a backdrop to your real life. It is the place God has sent you to bless.

articles.title: How to Use Technology Without Being Used by It
articles.excerpt: Your devices are not neutral tools waiting for your intentions. They are designed to capture your attention and sell it. Using them well begins by admitting they are using you.

articles.title: How to Be a Christian at Work
articles.excerpt: Being a Christian at work is mostly not about what you say. It is about the joints no one inspects. Here is how to live it Monday through Friday without becoming the office hypocrite.

articles.title: How to Discern Your Calling
articles.excerpt: Calling is not a secret God hides and dares you to find. It is mostly obedience in the place you already are. Here is how to discern it without losing your mind.

articles.title: How to Fight the Idol of Success
articles.excerpt: Success is the most respectable idol there is. Nobody warns you about it, because everyone is worshiping it. Here is how to see it and how to start tearing it down.

articles.title: How to Find Contentment With Enough
articles.excerpt: Contentment is not the absence of wanting. It is the presence of trust. Here is how to learn it, the way Paul said he had to learn it, because no one is born knowing how.

articles.title: How to Get Out of Debt
articles.excerpt: Debt is not just a financial state. It is a kind of bondage, and Scripture treats it as one. Here is a plan to get free, told without shame and without easy promises.

articles.title: How to Handle a Job Loss
articles.excerpt: Losing a job is not only a financial hit. It is a blow to your sense of who you are. Here is how to walk through it without being swallowed, and without pretending it is fine.

articles.title: How to Handle Money as a Couple
articles.excerpt: Money fights are rarely about money. They are about fear, control, and what you each believe security is. Here is how to handle money as one, not two people guarding two accounts.

articles.title: How to Make a Budget That Honors God
articles.excerpt: A budget is a moral document. It records what you actually love, not what you say you love. Here is how to build one that tells the truth and then bends toward God.

articles.title: How to Prepare for Retirement Faithfully
articles.excerpt: The Bible says to save like the ant and warns about the man who builds bigger barns to relax. Both are true. Here is how to prepare for the later years without serving the wrong god.

articles.title: How to Rest When You Feel You Cannot Stop
articles.excerpt: Sabbath is not a reward for finishing. It is a command you obey before the work is done. Here is how to stop when everything in you insists you cannot afford to.

articles.title: How to See Your Work as Worship
articles.excerpt: Work is not a punishment God invented after the fall. It was there in the garden first. Here is how to recover that, on a Monday, in a job you did not choose.

articles.title: How to Start Giving Generously
articles.excerpt: Generosity is not a feeling you wait for. It is a practice that produces the feeling. Here is how to begin, with a real number, this month, before you feel ready.
